standard.title: Develop safe dance practice and skills
standard.description: develop safe dance practice and use of expressive and technical skills and, as appropriate, genre- or style-specific techniques
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use technical and expressive skills with some control (AC9ADA6D01). They have not yet systematically extended movement vocabulary across diverse styles or applied safe dance practice principles deliberately across different physical demands.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop technical and expressive skills and movement vocabulary through sustained deliberate practice, applying safe dance practice principles appropriately.

nodes.label: Developing technical competence through deliberate practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop specific technical skills through deliberate practice, using feedback to guide improvement
nodes.minimum_width: Practise at least one technical skill (e.g. balance, alignment, coordination) with a clear improvement goal; describe what changed and how the improvement affects the dance
nodes.typical_width: Develop technical competence across multiple skills through sustained practice; use self, peer and teacher feedback to guide practice direction; document progress and remaining goals
wider: Extend technical competence across control, coordination, accuracy, alignment, balance, flexibility, strength and endurance — develop a personal practice plan targeting specific skills
Investigate how safe dance practice principles apply differently across styles and physical demands — develop own safe practice protocol
Experiment with style-specific techniques from a dance style distinct from own experience — document what the technique demands technically and how it extends own range

response_modes.reason: Technical skill development in dance is fundamentally a consolidation task — the skills (balance, alignment, coordination, strength) develop through sustained repetition with feedback, not through exposure to more contexts. Students who practise deliberately across a sustained period build genuine technical competence; students who rotate through many styles without sustained practice do not.

success_criteria: Practises at least one technical skill with a clear improvement goal
Describes what improved and how it affects the dance
Uses feedback from self, peer or teacher to direct practice

nodes.label: Extending movement vocabulary through diverse styles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can extend their movement vocabulary by experimenting with movements and techniques from diverse dance styles
nodes.minimum_width: Experiment with movements or techniques from at least one dance style beyond own familiar style; describe what the experimentation added to own movement vocabulary
nodes.typical_width: Improvise using movements and techniques from diverse dance styles; document what each style adds to available expressive range; reflect on how extended vocabulary informs own choreography and performance
wider: Develop a personal movement vocabulary archive — document movements and techniques from different styles with annotations about their expressive qualities and technical demands

Investigate how a specific dance style from another cultural context uses expressive skills (gesture, facial expression, use of space) differently — experiment with integrating these into own movement vocabulary
Create an improvisation that deliberately draws on movements from three or more distinct dance styles — evaluate how the combination creates new expressive possibilities

response_modes.reason: Students who improvise only within familiar movement vocabulary cannot access the expressive range the descriptor requires. Experimenting with diverse styles — each with different technical and expressive demands — genuinely expands what students can do and say through movement. Breadth here is the mechanism of growth, not just enrichment.

success_criteria: Experiments with at least one style beyond own familiar range
Describes what the experimentation added to own movement vocabulary
Movement vocabulary extension is connected to expressive possibility — not just technical novelty

nodes.label: Using expressive skills to communicate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use expressive skills — including gesture, facial expression and use of space — to communicate relationships, emotions or ideas in dance
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one expressive skill deliberately to communicate a relationship, emotion or idea; explain how the skill serves the communicative intent
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of expressive skills across a dance to communicate ideas with consistency and clarity; evaluate whether the expressive choices achieve the intended communication
wider: Explore how expressive skills carry different meanings in different cultural dance traditions — investigate and experiment with expanding own expressive range
Develop an extended improvisation focused entirely on expressive skills — gesture, facial expression, spatial relationship — without relying on technical virtuosity
Evaluate the difference between expressive skills that communicate clearly and those that are generic — develop criteria for evaluating own expressive choices

response_modes.reason: Students commonly use expressive skills by habit — smiling, making eye contact — without reasoning through whether those choices serve the intended communication. Scaffolding the reasoning (what am I trying to communicate, what expressive skill serves that, does the audience receive what I intend?) builds deliberate expressive practice rather than default behaviour.

success_criteria: Uses at least one expressive skill with a clear communicative purpose
Explains how the skill serves the intended communication
Does not rely on generic expression — choices are connected to specific intent
